title: Why Monbazillac tastes the way it does

lede.text: Mornings of mist or fog, then sunny afternoons, favour the noble rot that concentrates the grapes. These grapes give a sweet golden wine whose aromas are honey and acacia, with peach.

chapters.title: The left bank of the Dordogne
paras: The vineyard sits on the left bank of the Dordogne. Grapes are picked and the wine is made and aged in five communes of the Dordogne département: Colombier, Monbazillac, Pomport, Rouffignac-de-Sigoulès and Saint-Laurent-des-Vignes.
An area of twelve neighbouring communes may also make and age the wine. Bergerac and Sigoulès are among them.

fly.label: Monbazillac and its slopes
fly.caption: The vineyard lies on the left bank of the Dordogne, on slopes that face north.

fly.label: The Dordogne at Bergerac
fly.caption: The vineyard lies on the left bank of the Dordogne. Bergerac may make and age the wine.

chapters.title: Mist in the morning, sun in the afternoon
paras: Mornings of mist or fog are followed by sunny afternoons. This makes the vineyard well suited to grapes concentrated by Botrytis cinerea, the noble rot.
The grower's art is to pick the grapes, mostly Sémillon, at the best point of concentration. The harvest is by hand, in successive passes through the vines.

chapters.title: Clay-limestone facing north
paras: The vines cover clay-limestone slopes that face north.

chapters.title: Overripe grapes, picked pass by pass
paras: Monbazillac is a still white wine with residual sugar, above 45 g/l of fermentable sugar. The grapes are harvested overripe, with or without the action of noble rot.
Sémillon dominates. Sauvignon gris, Sauvignon blanc and Muscadelle are the other main grapes. Chenin, Ondenc and Ugni blanc are listed as secondary grapes.
Vines are planted at a minimum of 4000 per hectare, with at most 15 buds on each. Irrigation is forbidden, and yields top out at 40 hl/ha.
The whole grapes go into the press, which helps the juice come out. Ageing is needed for the wine to reach harmony and fullness.

The wine may carry the traditional mention Sélection de grains nobles, under rules set in the full specification. The label may also name the wider unit Sud-Ouest, in letters no larger than the appellation name.
